title: NGINX2Root: critical HTTP/2 flaws in NGINX allow unauthenticated code execution; F5 ships fixes
date_note: Wiz published its analysis on November 18; GBHackers followed on November 19. The F5 advisory date could not be read.
summary: F5 released updates for several NGINX flaws, including CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 in HTTP/2 handling, both listed at CVSS 4.0 9.2 (GBHackers attributes the score to F5). Wiz says it built proof-of-concept exploits but is not releasing them; neither source reports exploitation in the wild. Xint demonstrated chaining one flaw with a Linux kernel bug to gain root. Affected: NGINX 1.9.5 through 1.31.8 (CVE-2026-123007); fixed in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9.
plain: Serious flaws in the widely used NGINX web server could let an outsider run commands on it. Fixed versions are out; no attacks have been reported yet.
exec: NGINX fronts a large share of internet-facing sites; a remote code-execution flaw in default-style HTTP/2 setups puts web infrastructure at risk until patched.
action: Upgrade NGINX Open Source to 1.30.7 (stable) or 1.31.9 (mainline), or NGINX Plus to the fixed release in F5's advisory; if you cannot, set http2 off in affected server blocks (NGINX 1.25.1+) or remove the http2 parameter from listen directives. Check ingress-nginx against its own advisories.
impact: Unauthenticated code execution demonstrated by researchers; no in-the-wild exploitation reported.

validation.note: Wiz Research (a discoverer) and GBHackers agree on CVEs, versions and fixes. F5's advisory K000163928 would not render, so the vendor original was not read.
